title: England and Wales — inter-ethnic partnerships
definition: Among people living as part of a couple (married, civil partnership, or cohabiting), the share whose partner reports a different ethnic group. Endogamy = same ethnic group.
source: Office for National Statistics — 2011 Census analysis: What does the 2011 Census tell us about inter-ethnic relationships?
note: Overall 9% of people in couples were in an inter-ethnic relationship in 2011 (up from 7% in 2001). White British rates are low partly because the group is large. South Asian groups remain highly endogamous in marriage; cohabiting rates are much higher for the same groups. Census 2021 reports 5.7% of multi-person households had ethnic groups that differ within partnerships (a household, not person, measure).
